stem: Exactly one of 4 numbered boxes contains a prize, uniformly at random. You select box 1 without opening it. An inspector who does not know the prize location chooses one of boxes 2 through 4 uniformly at random, independently of the prize, and opens it. The opened box is empty. Given this observation, what is the probability the prize is in box 1?
author_derivation: After excluding prize/opened coincidences, box 1 appears in 3 of 9 equiprobable worlds.
intended_error: Use the unchanged probability from a knowledgeable host who deliberately avoids the prize.

stem: Four switches P, Q, R, S are each on or off. Exactly two are on. If P is on, Q is on. If Q is on, R is off. S is on if and only if exactly one of P and R is on. Which statement must be true in every configuration satisfying these rules?
answer: R and S are both on.
distractor: P and Q are both on.
author_derivation: P on would force Q and S on, violating exactly two. With P off, S=R; hence R,S on and Q off.
intended_error: Stop after satisfying the first implication without checking the global count and biconditional.

options.A: P and Q are both on.
options.B: R and S are both on.

stem: Independent binary inputs U and V satisfy P(U=1)=1/2 and P(V=1)=1/2. An alarm is 1 exactly when U=1 or V=1. You first observe alarm=1. intended_error: Replace the intervention with observing U=0 while the original alarm is 1.
